newsitem.title: UK: Working mums blamed for kids' school woes-UK study.
newsitem.headline: Working mums blamed for kids' school woes-UK study.

text.p: Children whose mothers work full time do worse at exams than those whose mothers work part-time, according to research published on Monday.

A North London University study of 600 familes in east London found that 11 percent of children with mothers in part-time work left school without passing any exams. But the figure rose to 25 percent among children whose mothers worked full time. All the famiies had fathers in full time work.
Researcher Margaret O'Brien identified a critical time immediately after school when children returned home and wanted to talk through their day.
"Mothers are key figures for education talk, for talking about homework, for discussing what has gone on in the day.
"It appears that for children who are living in households where the mother is working part-time, she's around more at that time of day when the children want to talk about these issues," she said.
Some parents' groups criticised the methodology and findings of the research, which focused on a deprived area of London.

"There may be other factors involved. We have found there is a very strong link between poverty and poor performance. If children don't have the conditions at home to study, they do badly," said Sally Witcher of the Child Poverty Action Group.
Wendy Rogers for the group Families Need Fathers said bringing up children was a joint responsibility for mothers and fathers.
"If fathers were encouraged more to take on their responsibilities inside the home, women would not be criticised so much for going out to work," she said.
